ex: Spettabile Ditta, con la presente si comunica che la fornitura subirà un ritardo di dieci giorni.
exEn: Dear Sirs, we hereby inform you that the delivery will be delayed by ten days.
note: Used only to address companies, offices and institutions in formal letters, usually abbreviated 'Spett.le' (never for people: for them use 'Egregio', 'Gentile').

en: most distinguished (title for a full professor)
ex: Chiarissimo Professore, Le scrivo per chiederLe la disponibilità a fare da relatore alla mia tesi.
exEn: Dear Professor, I am writing to ask whether you would be willing to supervise my thesis.
note: Traditional academic form of address for university professors, abbreviated 'Chiar.mo' / 'Chiar.ma'. 'Chiaro' here means 'illustrious', not 'clear'.

en: most esteemed (very formal form of address)
ex: Pregiatissimo Signor Sindaco, mi permetto di sottoporre alla Sua attenzione una questione urgente.
exEn: Most esteemed Mr Mayor, I take the liberty of bringing an urgent matter to your attention.
note: Abbreviated 'Preg.mo'. Extremely formal and slightly old-fashioned; 'Egregio' and 'Gentile' are the everyday formal openings. 'Pregiato' also means 'fine, valuable' (vini pregiati).

ex: La busta era indirizzata alla cortese attenzione del responsabile dell'ufficio legale.
exEn: The envelope was addressed for the attention of the head of the legal department.
note: Standard line on letters and emails, abbreviated 'c.a.' or 'Alla c.a. di'. Note the article contraction with the name that follows: 'alla cortese attenzione della dott.ssa Rossi'.

it: in attesa di un cortese riscontro
en: looking forward to hearing from you; awaiting your kind reply
ex: In attesa di un cortese riscontro, porgo distinti saluti.
exEn: Looking forward to your kind reply, I remain yours faithfully.
note: Fixed closing formula of formal correspondence; 'riscontro' is the bureaucratic word for 'reply, acknowledgement'. Variant: 'In attesa di un Suo gentile riscontro'.

en: not at all; don't mention it; by all means (formal)
ex: «La disturbo?» «Si figuri, si accomodi pure: stavo giusto per chiamarla.»
exEn: 'Am I disturbing you?' 'Not at all, do come in: I was just about to call you.'
note: Formal (Lei) counterpart of 'figurati'. Used both to wave away thanks or apologies and to grant permission. Literally 'imagine (that)!'; the more emphatic version is 'ma si figuri!'.

en: of course; by all means; heaven forbid
ex: «Posso portare mia moglie alla cena?» «Ci mancherebbe altro, siete entrambi invitati.»
exEn: 'May I bring my wife to the dinner?' 'Of course, you are both invited.'
note: Emphatic form of 'ci mancherebbe'. Two opposite uses depending on context: enthusiastic assent ('of course, it goes without saying') or indignant rejection ('that would be the last straw!'). Tone decides.

ex: Il cardinale attraversò la navata nella sua veste scarlatta.
exEn: The cardinal walked down the nave in his scarlet robe.
note: Bright red with an orange tinge; historically the colour of cardinals and of 'la lettera scarlatta'. 'Scarlattina' (scarlet fever) derives from it. Compare 'cremisi' (deep crimson) and 'vermiglio'.

ex: Nell'antica Roma la porpora era riservata ai senatori e all'imperatore.
exEn: In ancient Rome purple was reserved for senators and the emperor.
note: As a colour adjective it is invariable ('tende color porpora'). Historically a reddish purple made from murex shellfish; hence 'porporato' = cardinal. Modern 'purple' in everyday speech is 'viola'.

ex: Il tramonto virava dall'arancio all'indaco sopra la laguna.
exEn: The sunset was shifting from orange to indigo over the lagoon.
note: Invariable as an adjective ('jeans indaco'); as a noun (masc.) it is the dye extracted from the Indigofera plant, used for denim. One of the seven colours of the rainbow in the Italian tradition.

ex: La ceramica di Deruta è celebre per i suoi decori in blu cobalto.
exEn: Deruta pottery is famous for its cobalt blue decorations.
note: 'Blu cobalto' is an intense, slightly violet blue; the metal itself (Co) is also 'cobalto'. As a colour adjective it is invariable: 'occhi cobalto'.

ex: La carta traslucida lascia passare la luce ma non permette di distinguere le forme.
exEn: Translucent paper lets light through but does not allow shapes to be made out.
note: Precise term between 'trasparente' (see-through) and 'opaco' (opaque). 'Diafano' is the literary near-synonym, also used of pale skin.

ex: Aveva una barba rossiccia che tradiva le origini irlandesi.
exEn: He had a ginger beard that betrayed his Irish origins.
note: The suffix '-iccio' gives an approximate, often slightly disparaging shade: rossiccio, giallognolo, verdognolo, grigiastro, biancastro, nerastro. Of hair 'rosso' or 'fulvo' are neutral.

ex: Le pagine del manoscritto avevano assunto una tinta giallognola.
exEn: The pages of the manuscript had taken on a yellowish tint.
note: The suffix '-ognolo' ('verdognolo', 'amarognolo') marks an imprecise or unpleasant shade; of complexion it suggests ill health ('un colorito giallognolo').

ex: Una luce biancastra filtrava dalle persiane socchiuse.
exEn: A whitish light filtered through the half-closed shutters.
note: '-astro' is the most pejorative of the colour suffixes (grigiastro, verdastro, nerastro, rossastro): a dull, impure version of the colour. Neutral 'off-white' for paint is 'bianco sporco' or 'avorio'.

ex: La luna gettava un riflesso argenteo sulle acque immobili del lago.
exEn: The moon cast a silvery reflection on the still waters of the lake.
note: Literary/descriptive; the plain adjective is 'argentato' (silver-plated) or 'color argento'. Same pattern: 'aureo' / 'dorato' (golden), 'bronzeo' (bronze-coloured), 'ferreo' (iron-like, figurative).

ex: Lo smalto madreperlaceo cambia riflesso a seconda dell'inclinazione della luce.
exEn: The pearly nail polish changes its sheen depending on the angle of the light.
note: From 'madreperla' (mother-of-pearl). Suffix '-aceo' = 'resembling': 'perlaceo', 'violaceo' (purplish), 'rosaceo', 'cartaceo' (paper-based).

ex: Il pittore ha usato tutte le gradazioni del blu, dal celeste al blu notte.
exEn: The painter used every gradation of blue, from sky blue to midnight blue.
note: Both a scale of shades and 'gradazione alcolica' (alcohol content); 'tonalità' is a single tone, 'sfumatura' a subtle nuance. Also in linguistics: 'gradazione dell'aggettivo' (degrees of comparison).

ex: Le piastrelle romboidali creano un effetto ottico tridimensionale sul pavimento.
exEn: The diamond-shaped tiles create a three-dimensional optical effect on the floor.
note: From 'rombo' (rhombus). Other shape adjectives in '-oidale' / '-ico': 'trapezoidale', 'ellissoidale', 'sferico', 'cubico', 'conico', 'cilindrico', 'esagonale'.

ex: Il sasso produsse una serie di cerchi concentrici sulla superficie dello stagno.
exEn: The stone produced a series of concentric circles on the surface of the pond.
note: Opposite: 'eccentrico' (in geometry, off-centre; of people, eccentric). Frequent in 'cerchi concentrici' and in urban planning ('sviluppo concentrico della città').

ex: Ho scelto un tavolo con gli angoli smussati per la sicurezza dei bambini.
exEn: I chose a table with rounded-off corners for the children's safety.
note: From 'smussare' (to bevel, to take the edge off). Figurative: 'smussare gli angoli' = to smooth things over, 'toni smussati' = softened tones. Opposite: 'spigoloso', 'appuntito'.

ex: La torre medievale era tozza e massiccia, costruita più per difendere che per stupire.
exEn: The medieval tower was squat and massive, built more to defend than to impress.
note: Of objects, buildings and body build: short and thick ('dita tozze'). Opposite 'slanciato' (slender, soaring). Homonym: 'un tozzo di pane' = a crust of bread ('per un tozzo di pane' = for next to nothing).

ex: Le colonne slanciate della cattedrale gotica sembrano sfidare la gravità.
exEn: The soaring columns of the Gothic cathedral seem to defy gravity.
note: Positive in tone: 'una figura slanciata' is elegant, whereas 'magro' is neutral and 'allampanato' is lanky. Opposite: 'tozzo', 'tarchiato' (stocky, of people).

ex: Il quoziente familiare terrebbe conto del numero di figli nel calcolo delle imposte.
exEn: The family quotient would take the number of children into account when calculating taxes.
note: Result of a division ('dividendo, divisore, quoziente, resto'). Common compounds: 'quoziente intellettivo' (IQ), 'quoziente familiare' (tax policy).

ex: Se avesse avuto un briciolo di buon senso, non avrebbe firmato senza leggere.
exEn: If he had had an ounce of common sense, he would not have signed without reading.
note: Almost always 'un briciolo di' + abstract noun (buon senso, dignità, fortuna), mostly in negative or hypothetical sentences. 'Briciola' is the literal crumb; 'le briciole' = scraps, leftovers.

ex: Il dato è calcolato con un'approssimazione di più o meno due punti percentuali.
exEn: The figure is calculated with an approximation of plus or minus two percentage points.
note: Note the ambiguity: 'per approssimazione' = by successive attempts; 'con approssimazione' (of a person's work) = carelessly, imprecisely. 'Approssimativo' = rough / sloppy.

ex: L'arrotondamento per eccesso dei prezzi al momento del passaggio all'euro fece discutere a lungo.
exEn: The rounding up of prices at the time of the switch to the euro was debated for a long time.
note: 'Arrotondamento per eccesso' = rounding up, 'per difetto' = rounding down. The verb 'arrotondare' also means to top up one's income ('arrotondare lo stipendio').

ex: Facciamo cifra tonda: cento euro e non se ne parla più.
exEn: Let's make it a round figure: a hundred euros and that's the end of it.
note: Also 'numero tondo'. 'Fare cifra tonda' is what you say when settling a price or a bill informally. 'In cifra tonda' = in round figures.

ex: Lo scarto tra i due candidati è stato di appena trecento voti.
exEn: The gap between the two candidates was just three hundred votes.
note: Polysemous: numerical gap ('scarto quadratico medio' = standard deviation), factory rejects ('materiale di scarto'), a sudden swerve ('uno scarto di lato'), and discarded cards. 'Scarto generazionale' = generation gap.

ex: La media ponderata degli esami tiene conto del numero di crediti di ciascuno.
exEn: The weighted average of the exams takes into account the number of credits of each one.
note: Central in Italian universities, where the final degree mark is based on the 'media ponderata' of exam marks. 'Media aritmetica' = simple mean; 'ponderare' = to weigh up.

ex: In vent'anni il prezzo delle case in centro è salito al quintuplo.
exEn: In twenty years the price of houses in the centre has risen fivefold.
note: Series: doppio, triplo, quadruplo, quintuplo, sestuplo, decuplo, centuplo. Used as noun with the article: 'il quintuplo di'. Verb: 'quintuplicare'.

ex: Il bagaglio in eccesso viene addebitato a un costo di dodici euro al chilo.
exEn: Excess baggage is charged at a cost of twelve euros per kilo.
note: Follows the noun: 'peso in eccesso', 'liquidità in eccesso'. 'Per eccesso' (rounding up) is a different phrase; 'eccedenza' is the noun for the surplus itself.

ex: Con quello stipendio arrivava a malapena alla fine del mese.
exEn: On that salary he barely made it to the end of the month.
note: Also spelled 'a mala pena'. Stronger and more literary than 'appena'; 'a stento' is the close synonym ('a stento' stresses effort, 'a malapena' stresses insufficiency).

ex: Ho ricevuto un'infinità di messaggi dopo l'intervista in televisione.
exEn: I received countless messages after the interview on television.
note: Hyperbolic quantifier followed by 'di'; register neutral to colloquial. Near-synonyms: 'una miriade di' (more literary), 'un sacco di' (colloquial), 'una marea di'.

ex: La sovrabbondanza di informazioni finisce per paralizzare la capacità di decidere.
exEn: The overabundance of information ends up paralysing the capacity to decide.
note: Prefix 'sovra-' / 'sopra-' = over-, excess: sovrappeso, sovraffollamento, sovrapproduzione. Adjective 'sovrabbondante'; in economics 'eccedenza' or 'surplus' are the technical terms.

ex: La scarsità di risorse idriche costringerà molte regioni a rivedere le colture.
exEn: The scarcity of water resources will force many regions to reconsider their crops.
note: Economic key term ('il principio della scarsità'). Distinguish: 'carenza' (deficiency, lack of something needed), 'penuria' (dearth, literary), 'mancanza' (absence).

ex: L'importo complessivo della fattura, IVA inclusa, è di duemilaquattrocento euro.
exEn: The total amount of the invoice, including VAT, is two thousand four hundred euros.
note: Bureaucratic/commercial word for a sum of money; 'somma' and 'cifra' are the everyday equivalents. Collocations: 'importo lordo/netto', 'per un importo pari a'.

ex: Il reddito della famiglia è appena sotto la soglia di povertà fissata dall'ISTAT.
exEn: The family's income is just below the poverty threshold set by ISTAT.
note: Literal doorstep and figurative limit: 'soglia di povertà', 'soglia del dolore', 'soglia di attenzione', 'alle soglie della pensione' (on the verge of retirement).

ex: I medici hanno diagnosticato una cataratta incipiente all'occhio destro.
exEn: The doctors diagnosed an incipient cataract in the right eye.
note: Formal/medical-literary: 'calvizie incipiente', 'crisi incipiente'. 'Incipit' (the opening words of a text) shares the same root.

ex: L'intempestiva uscita del ministro ha fatto crollare i titoli bancari in borsa.
exEn: The minister's ill-timed remark sent bank shares tumbling on the stock exchange.
note: Opposite of 'tempestivo' (prompt, timely). Note that 'intempestivo' means badly timed rather than late: for 'late' use 'tardivo'.

ex: Il giudice ha concesso il differimento della pena per motivi di salute.
exEn: The judge granted a deferral of the sentence on health grounds.
note: Legal-bureaucratic nominalisation of 'differire' (to defer). Near-synonyms: 'rinvio' (adjournment, general), 'proroga' (extension of a deadline), 'dilazione' (extension for payment).

ex: Tengo uno scadenzario dettagliato di tasse, bollette e rinnovi per non pagare mai una mora.
exEn: I keep a detailed schedule of taxes, bills and renewals so that I never pay a late fee.
note: Accounting term ('scadenzario clienti/fornitori') that has entered everyday organisational language. Related: 'scadenza' (deadline), 'scadenzato' (spread over set dates).

ex: La periodicità dei controlli è fissata dalla legge in base al tipo di impianto.
exEn: The frequency of inspections is fixed by law according to the type of installation.
note: Formal; 'con periodicità mensile' = on a monthly basis. Do not confuse with 'frequenza' (how often, or attendance). 'Periodico' = a periodical / magazine.

ex: Le luci intermittenti del cantiere lampeggiavano nella nebbia.
exEn: The intermittent lights of the building site were flashing in the fog.
note: Also of phenomena and work: 'pioggia intermittente', 'lavoro intermittente' (on-call contract), 'digiuno intermittente'. 'A intermittenza' = on and off; 'saltuario' = occasional.

ex: I contatti tra i due fratelli si erano ridotti a sporadiche telefonate.
exEn: Contact between the two brothers had dwindled to sporadic phone calls.
note: Stronger than 'occasionale', suggests rarity and irregularity ('casi sporadici'). Medical: 'forma sporadica' = non-hereditary. Adverb 'sporadicamente'.

ex: Il crollo del ponte fu causato da una serie di fattori concomitanti.
exEn: The bridge collapse was caused by a series of concomitant factors.
note: Formal; 'cause concomitanti' in law and medicine, 'in concomitanza con' = at the same time as. 'Concorrente' as adjective has a similar sense in legal texts ('colpa concorrente').

ex: Alla vigilia delle elezioni i sondaggi davano i due schieramenti praticamente alla pari.
exEn: On the eve of the elections the polls had the two coalitions practically neck and neck.
note: Frequent in journalism, often loosely meaning 'shortly before'. Also 'essere alla vigilia di' (to be on the brink of). 'La vigilia' alone = Christmas Eve.

en: the day after; in the aftermath of
ex: All'indomani del referendum il governo rassegnò le dimissioni.
exEn: The day after the referendum the government resigned.
note: Written/journalistic; 'l'indomani' alone = the next day (narrative past, unlike 'domani'). Extended sense: 'all'indomani della guerra' = in the aftermath of the war.

ex: Partirono sul far del giorno, quando la nebbia ancora avvolgeva la valle.
exEn: They set off at daybreak, when the mist still shrouded the valley.
note: Literary; parallel 'sul far della sera/della notte' (at nightfall). Same construction as 'sull'imbrunire' and 'al calar del sole'. Neutral: 'all'alba'.

ex: Agli albori del cinema le proiezioni duravano pochi minuti.
exEn: In the earliest days of cinema screenings lasted a few minutes.
note: Plural-only in the figurative sense ('agli albori di', 'fin dagli albori'). Literary singular 'albore' = first light. Related: 'alba' (dawn), 'albeggiare' (to dawn).

en: staggered; spread out over time; in instalments
ex: Per evitare assembramenti gli ingressi sono stati scaglionati nell'arco della mattinata.
exEn: To avoid crowds, entry was staggered over the course of the morning.
note: From 'scaglione' (echelon, bracket: 'scaglioni di reddito' = income brackets). 'Scaglionare' = to stagger payments, entries, holidays. Adverb: 'a scaglioni'.

en: at full capacity; fully operational; in steady state
ex: Una volta a regime, l'impianto tratterà duecento tonnellate di rifiuti al giorno.
exEn: Once fully operational, the plant will process two hundred tonnes of waste a day.
note: Technical-managerial phrase: 'andare a regime', 'entrare a regime' = to reach full operating capacity. 'Regime' also means diet ('regime alimentare') and political regime.

ex: L'aumento sarà corrisposto con effetto retroattivo dal primo gennaio.
exEn: The pay rise will be paid with retroactive effect from the first of January.
note: Legal principle: 'la legge non ha effetto retroattivo' (irretroattività della legge). Noun 'retroattività'; adverb 'retroattivamente'.

en: twenty-year period; (il Ventennio) the Fascist era
ex: Nell'ultimo ventennio il numero di laureati è quasi raddoppiato.
exEn: In the last twenty years the number of graduates has almost doubled.
note: Capitalised 'il Ventennio' refers specifically to Fascist rule (1922-1943). Series: biennio, triennio, quinquennio, decennio, ventennio, trentennio; 'ventennale' = twentieth anniversary / lasting twenty years.

ex: Il tribunale ha ammesso solo i documenti antecedenti alla firma del contratto.
exEn: The court admitted only documents prior to the signing of the contract.
note: Formal synonym of 'precedente', used with 'a'. As a noun: 'gli antecedenti' (background, precedents) and, in grammar, the antecedent of a relative pronoun. Opposite: 'susseguente', 'successivo'.

en: woman's suit (jacket and skirt or trousers)
ex: Si presentò al colloquio con un tailleur blu scuro impeccabile.
exEn: She turned up at the interview in an impeccable dark blue suit.
note: French loanword, invariable, pronounced roughly 'taiér'. 'Tailleur pantalone' = trouser suit. The man's suit is 'completo' or 'abito'.

ex: Il direttore d'orchestra entrò in frac tra gli applausi del pubblico.
exEn: The conductor entered in a tailcoat to the applause of the audience.
note: Invariable. Ladder of men's formal wear: 'abito scuro' < 'smoking' (dinner jacket) < 'tight' (morning coat) < 'frac' (tailcoat, the most formal). 'In frac' = in white tie.

ex: Le indossatrici sfilarono con i capi della nuova collezione autunno-inverno.
exEn: The models paraded in the garments of the new autumn-winter collection.
note: From 'indossare' (to wear). Today the anglicism 'modello/modella' is far more common; 'indossatrice' survives in formal or older usage. 'Fotomodella' = photographic model.

ex: Non spende cifre folli per le griffe: preferisce capi anonimi ma ben tagliati.
exEn: She does not spend crazy sums on designer labels: she prefers anonymous but well-cut garments.
note: French loan (literally 'claw' or 'signature'), invariable, pronounced 'grif'. Derivatives: 'griffato' (designer, branded), 'capi griffati'. 'Marca' is the general word for brand.

ex: La Guardia di Finanza ha sequestrato migliaia di borse frutto di contraffazione.
exEn: The finance police seized thousands of bags produced by counterfeiting.
note: Legal term for fake branded goods, currency and documents; adjective 'contraffatto'. Colloquial 'tarocco' / 'taroccato' = fake, knock-off; 'falso' is the generic word.

ex: Un maglione di cachemire vale l'investimento solo se lo si lava a mano con cura.
exEn: A cashmere sweater is worth the investment only if you hand-wash it carefully.
note: French spelling is standard in Italian (also 'cashmere'); pronounced 'casc-mir'. Fine fibres: cachemire, alpaca, mohair, angora, lana merino.

ex: La fodera della giacca è in raso di seta color champagne.
exEn: The lining of the jacket is in champagne-coloured silk satin.
note: Satin weave, glossy on one side. As an adjective 'raso' = level, flush ('un cucchiaio raso' = a level spoonful, 'raso terra' = at ground level) and, of fabric, smooth ('velluto raso').

ex: Le maniche in organza davano all'abito da sposa una leggerezza quasi impalpabile.
exEn: The organza sleeves gave the wedding dress an almost impalpable lightness.
note: Sheer, stiff fabric of silk or synthetic fibre. Group of sheer fabrics: organza, tulle, chiffon, voile, mussola (muslin).

ex: Le pareti del salone erano rivestite di damasco rosso, secondo il gusto ottocentesco.
exEn: The walls of the drawing room were covered in red damask, in nineteenth-century taste.
note: Named after Damascus; patterned fabric used for upholstery, curtains and formal garments. 'Damascato' = damask-patterned; 'damaschinatura' is the metal inlay technique.

ex: La gonna plissettata è tornata di moda dopo decenni di oblio.
exEn: The pleated skirt has come back into fashion after decades of oblivion.
note: From French 'plissé' (also used unchanged: 'gonna plissé'). 'Piega' = pleat or crease; 'a pieghe' is the plain equivalent. Iconic: the 'plissé' of Fortuny and Issey Miyake.

en: collar (of a coat or jacket); lapel
ex: Alzò il bavero del cappotto contro il vento gelido.
exEn: He turned up the collar of his coat against the icy wind.
note: Refers to the collar of outer garments; 'colletto' is a shirt collar, 'risvolto' the lapel proper. Idiom: 'prendere qualcuno per il bavero' = to grab someone by the collar / to make fun of them.

ex: Per il matrimonio ha indossato i gemelli d'oro ereditati dal nonno.
exEn: For the wedding he wore the gold cufflinks inherited from his grandfather.
note: Plural-only in this sense (singular 'gemello' = twin). Used with shirts 'con polsino doppio' or 'alla francese'. Also 'fermacravatta' (tie clip), 'spilla' (brooch).

ex: A ottobre basta un soprabito leggero; il cappotto pesante può aspettare.
exEn: In October a light overcoat is enough; the heavy coat can wait.
note: Lighter than a 'cappotto', for mid-season. Family: 'spolverino' (duster coat), 'trench', 'impermeabile' (raincoat), 'mantella' (cape), 'giaccone' (heavy jacket).

ex: Il notaio portava sempre un panciotto con l'orologio da taschino.
exEn: The notary always wore a waistcoat with a pocket watch.
note: Somewhat old-fashioned or ironic; the neutral term is 'gilet'. From 'pancia' (belly). The 'orologio da taschino' with chain is its classic accessory.

ex: Arrivò alla riunione con la camicia sgualcita, come se avesse dormito vestito.
exEn: He arrived at the meeting with his shirt crumpled, as if he had slept in his clothes.
note: From 'sgualcire'. Near-synonyms: 'stropicciato' (rumpled by rubbing), 'spiegazzato' (badly creased), 'stazzonato' (literary). Opposite 'stirato' (ironed), 'inamidato' (starched).

ex: Portava sempre la stessa giacca, lisa ai gomiti ma di ottimo taglio.
exEn: He always wore the same jacket, threadbare at the elbows but beautifully cut.
note: Specifically of fabric worn thin by rubbing ('liso ai gomiti', 'un tappeto liso'). 'Logoro' is broader (worn out, also figurative); 'consunto' is literary; 'sdrucito' = torn at the seams.

ex: Il divano era ormai logoro, ma nessuno in famiglia voleva separarsene.
exEn: The sofa was worn out by now, but nobody in the family wanted to part with it.
note: From 'logorare' (to wear out; 'logorarsi' = to wear oneself out). Figurative: 'un'espressione logora' (hackneyed), 'nervi logori', 'guerra di logoramento' (war of attrition).

en: to be a spendthrift; money slips through one's fingers
ex: Con lo stipendio che prende potrebbe risparmiare, ma ha le mani bucate.
exEn: On the salary he earns he could save, but money just slips through his fingers.
note: Literally 'to have holes in one's hands'. Opposite: 'essere tirchio', 'avere il braccino corto' (to be stingy). Related: 'spendaccione' (big spender).

en: to bear a grudge; to have it in for someone
ex: Da quando è stato escluso dalla squadra ha il dente avvelenato con l'allenatore.
exEn: Ever since he was dropped from the team he has had it in for the coach.
note: Followed by 'con' or 'contro' + person. Image of a poisoned tooth ready to bite. Synonyms: 'serbare rancore', 'avercela con qualcuno' (milder).

en: to be thick-skinned; to be tough
ex: Le critiche non la scalfiscono: dopo vent'anni di politica ha la pelle dura.
exEn: Criticism does not touch her: after twenty years in politics she is thick-skinned.
note: Also 'avere le spalle larghe' (to be able to take it). Opposite: 'essere permaloso' (touchy), 'avere la pelle sottile'. 'Duro a morire' = die-hard.

en: to have an obsession; to have a one-track mind
ex: Da mesi ha un chiodo fisso: comprare una casa al mare a qualunque costo.
exEn: For months he has had one obsession: buying a house by the sea at any cost.
note: Also 'essere un chiodo fisso' of the idea itself. Verb 'fissarsi' (to get fixated); noun 'fissazione', 'fissa' (colloquial: 'ha la fissa del calcio').

it: mettere il carro davanti ai buoi
en: to put the cart before the horse
ex: Parlare di assunzioni prima di aver trovato i finanziamenti è mettere il carro davanti ai buoi.
exEn: Talking about hiring before having found the funding is putting the cart before the horse.
note: Note the oxen ('buoi') instead of the English horse. Similar: 'vendere la pelle dell'orso prima di averlo ucciso' (to count one's chickens).

en: to plant a seed of doubt; to put a bee in someone's bonnet
ex: Quel commento del collega mi ha messo la pulce nell'orecchio: e se il progetto fosse già stato bocciato?
exEn: That remark from my colleague planted a seed of doubt: what if the project had already been rejected?
note: Literally 'to put a flea in the ear': to arouse suspicion or curiosity. Construction: 'mettere la pulce nell'orecchio a qualcuno'.

en: to cover oneself; to hedge; to make excuses in advance
ex: Prima ancora di iniziare la relazione ha messo le mani avanti, dicendo che i dati erano incompleti.
exEn: Before even starting his report he covered himself, saying the data was incomplete.
note: Image of stretching out one's hands to break a fall. Used of pre-emptive justifications; 'pararsi il sedere' is the vulgar equivalent.

en: to get the wrong end of the stick; to misunderstand completely
ex: Ha preso fischi per fiaschi: nessuno voleva licenziarlo, gli stavano offrendo un trasferimento.
exEn: He got the wrong end of the stick: nobody wanted to fire him, they were offering him a transfer.
note: Play on the similar-sounding 'fischi' (whistles) and 'fiaschi' (flasks). Also 'prendere lucciole per lanterne' (same meaning, 'fireflies for lanterns').

en: to catch someone red-handed; to catch out
ex: Il giornalista ha preso in castagna il ministro, che aveva citato dati inventati.
exEn: The journalist caught the minister out: he had quoted invented figures.
note: Probably from 'castagna' as an old word for a blunder. Synonyms: 'cogliere in fallo', 'cogliere sul fatto', 'beccare' (colloquial), 'con le mani nel sacco'.

it: prendere il toro per le corna
en: to take the bull by the horns
ex: Invece di rimandare, ha preso il toro per le corna e ha chiesto un aumento al direttore.
exEn: Instead of putting it off, she took the bull by the horns and asked the director for a raise.
note: Same image as English. Related: 'affrontare di petto' (to face head-on), 'tagliare la testa al toro' (to settle a matter once and for all).

en: to take the lion's share; to dominate
ex: Nel bilancio regionale la sanità fa la parte del leone, assorbendo tre quarti delle risorse.
exEn: In the regional budget health care takes the lion's share, absorbing three quarters of the resources.
note: From Aesop's fable. Frequent in economic and political journalism. Also 'la parte del leone' as a noun phrase: 'si è preso la parte del leone'.

en: to reckon without one's host; to overlook a crucial factor
ex: Pensavano di vincere facile, ma avevano fatto i conti senza l'oste: gli avversari erano preparatissimi.
exEn: They thought they would win easily, but they had reckoned without their host: their opponents were extremely well prepared.
note: The innkeeper ('oste') presents the bill you did not expect. Used when a plan ignores a decisive party or obstacle.

en: to play dumb; to pretend not to know
ex: Quando gli ho chiesto dei soldi mancanti ha fatto lo gnorri.
exEn: When I asked him about the missing money he played dumb.
note: 'Gnorri' is a made-up name from 'ignorare'. Colloquial synonyms: 'fare il finto tonto', 'fare l'indiano', 'cascare dalle nuvole' (to act surprised).

en: to be contrary; to disagree for the sake of it
ex: Non ha vere obiezioni: fa il bastian contrario per il gusto di discutere.
exEn: He has no real objections: he is being contrary for the pleasure of arguing.
note: 'Bastian contrario' (from the name Sebastiano) is also a noun: 'è un bastian contrario'. Neutral equivalents: 'contestatore', 'polemico'.

en: to bend over backwards; to go to great lengths
ex: Con due lavori e tre figli fa i salti mortali per arrivare a fine mese.
exEn: With two jobs and three children she bends over backwards to make ends meet.
note: Literally 'to do somersaults'. Similar: 'farsi in quattro' (to go out of one's way), 'fare carte false' (to do anything, even illegal, to get something).

en: to draw a blank; to achieve nothing
ex: Le ricerche del disperso sono durate una settimana, ma hanno fatto un buco nell'acqua.
exEn: The search for the missing man lasted a week, but drew a blank.
note: Image of a pointless action (you cannot make a hole in water). Also 'un buco nell'acqua' as a noun phrase = a flop, a failure.

en: to give someone a hard time; to be a tough opponent
ex: La squadra neopromossa ha dato filo da torcere ai campioni in carica.
exEn: The newly promoted team gave the reigning champions a hard time.
note: From the difficulty of twisting ('torcere') thread. Used of competitors, problems, children: 'un bambino che dà filo da torcere'.

en: to talk nonsense; to be off one's head
ex: Se pensi di finire il trasloco in un pomeriggio, stai dando i numeri.
exEn: If you think you can finish the move in one afternoon, you are off your head.
note: From the lottery 'numeri' supposedly revealed by people in a trance. Colloquial; synonyms 'sragionare', 'essere fuori di testa', 'vaneggiare'.

en: to shoot oneself in the foot
ex: Rivelando quel dettaglio in tribunale, l'imputato si è dato la zappa sui piedi.
exEn: By revealing that detail in court, the defendant shot himself in the foot.
note: Literally 'to hit one's own feet with the hoe'. Reflexive construction: 'mi sono dato la zappa sui piedi'.

en: to go swimmingly; to be going great
ex: Gli affari vanno a gonfie vele da quando abbiamo aperto il negozio online.
exEn: Business has been going swimmingly since we opened the online shop.
note: Sailing image: full sails. Opposite: 'andare a rotoli' (to go to pieces), 'andare a monte' (to fall through).

en: to be over the moon; to go into raptures
ex: Ogni volta che il nipotino la chiama «nonna» va in brodo di giuggiole.
exEn: Every time her little grandson calls her 'grandma' she goes into raptures.
note: 'Giuggiole' are jujubes, a sweet fruit. Usually affectionate or mildly ironic about someone's delight.

en: to drag on; to take a long time
ex: La causa civile rischia di andare per le lunghe: la prima udienza è fissata tra due anni.
exEn: The civil case is likely to drag on: the first hearing is set for two years' time.
note: Neutral register, very common in speech and writing. Related: 'tirarla per le lunghe' (to string something out), 'lungaggini' (delays).

en: to fall through; to come to nothing
ex: Il matrimonio è andato a monte a due settimane dalla cerimonia.
exEn: The wedding fell through two weeks before the ceremony.
note: From card games ('andare a monte' = to cancel the hand). Transitive: 'mandare a monte un progetto' (to wreck a plan). Synonym 'saltare', 'sfumare'.

en: to be riding high; to be at the peak of success
ex: Negli anni Novanta il regista era sulla cresta dell'onda e ogni film era un successo.
exEn: In the nineties the director was riding high and every film was a hit.
note: Surfing image, common for celebrities and companies. Opposite: 'essere in declino', 'essere finito nel dimenticatoio' (to be forgotten).

en: to be penniless; to be on the streets
ex: Dopo il fallimento dell'azienda la famiglia si è ritrovata sul lastrico.
exEn: After the company's bankruptcy the family found itself on the streets.
note: 'Lastrico' = pavement. Also 'ridurre qualcuno sul lastrico' (to ruin someone), 'finire sul lastrico'. Stronger than 'essere al verde' (to be broke).

en: to have an ace up one's sleeve
ex: L'avvocato aveva ancora un asso nella manica: un testimone che nessuno si aspettava.
exEn: The lawyer still had an ace up his sleeve: a witness nobody was expecting.
note: Also 'tirare fuori l'asso dalla manica'. Card-game idioms: 'giocare l'ultima carta', 'scoprire le carte', 'avere buone carte in mano'.

en: to be born lucky; to be born with a silver spoon
ex: Trova sempre parcheggio sotto casa: quello è nato con la camicia.
exEn: He always finds a parking space right outside his house: that man was born lucky.
note: From babies born still wrapped in the amniotic sac, a sign of good fortune. Usually in the past participle: 'è nato con la camicia'.

en: to be in deep trouble; to be up to one's neck
ex: Con tre rate arretrate e la scadenza delle tasse, ha l'acqua alla gola.
exEn: With three overdue instalments and taxes due, he is up to his neck.
note: Mostly financial or time pressure. Related: 'essere alle strette' (to be cornered), 'essere con le spalle al muro'.

it: non essere farina del proprio sacco
en: not to be one's own work; to be borrowed or plagiarised
ex: Il discorso era brillante, ma si capiva che non era farina del suo sacco.
exEn: The speech was brilliant, but it was clear it was not his own work.
note: Literally 'flour from one's own sack'. Adjust the possessive: 'del suo/tuo/mio sacco'. Used of ideas, texts, jokes.

en: to come at just the right moment
ex: Quel bonifico è capitato a fagiolo: proprio il giorno in cui scadeva l'affitto.
exEn: That bank transfer came at just the right moment: the very day the rent was due.
note: Also 'cascare a fagiolo', 'arrivare a fagiolo'. Colloquial; 'a proposito' and 'al momento giusto' are the neutral equivalents.

en: to jump out of the frying pan into the fire
ex: Ha lasciato un capo tirannico per uno ancora peggiore: è caduto dalla padella nella brace.
exEn: He left a tyrannical boss for an even worse one: he jumped out of the frying pan into the fire.
note: 'Brace' = embers. Also 'passare dalla padella alla brace'. Note the Italian falls into embers, not fire.
